---
title: "A3 exercises — Exchange, blood and flow"
---

Refer to the [tutorial](index.qmd). Values are simplified invented examples.
Allow 60–90 minutes; leave with a transport-path diagram, calculations with
units and a comparative explanation. No physiological recording is requested.

## 1. Separate transport processes

Trace oxygen from environmental air to a mammalian muscle mitochondrion.
For each arrow, state whether the main process is bulk flow, diffusion or
binding/unbinding. Then identify how the route differs in an insect.

Where would a thickened exchange barrier act? Where would reduced ventilation
act? Why need not increasing heart rate correct either problem completely?

## 2. Compare barriers quantitatively

Hold diffusion properties constant and use $\dot M\propto A\Delta P/L$.
A hypothetical exchange surface has area 10 units, thickness 2 units and
gradient 4 units. A second has twice the area, twice the thickness and half
the gradient. Calculate the second surface's predicted transfer rate relative
to the first. Explain which variables were held fixed.

What does the calculation omit about a real heterogeneous organ with flowing
fluids? Give one example.

## 3. Keep local countercurrent gradients explicit

The invented values below represent partial pressures in compatible units
at positions along a gill. Water moves from left to right; blood moves from
right to left. Values are schematic and are not a fitted physiological model.

| Position, left → right | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Water oxygen partial pressure | 100 | 80 | 60 | 40 |
| Blood oxygen partial pressure | 90 | 70 | 50 | 30 |

Draw both flow arrows and mark diffusion direction at each position. Identify
the water inlet/outlet and blood inlet/outlet. Explain why blood leaving with
a value of 90 does not mean oxygen diffused uphill from water leaving at 40.
Which values must be compared locally?

## 4. Calculate oxygen use and cardiac output

In a hypothetical steady state, blood flow is 4 L min⁻¹, arterial oxygen
content 190 mL O₂ L⁻¹ and venous content 140 mL O₂ L⁻¹. Calculate oxygen
use. Heart rate is 80 beats min⁻¹ and stroke volume 0.050 L beat⁻¹: verify
the flow using those values.

Then use an activity state of heart rate 120 beats min⁻¹, stroke volume
0.080 L beat⁻¹ and arterial–venous difference 100 mL O₂ L⁻¹. Calculate
output and oxygen use. State why inserting oxygen partial pressures instead
of contents would be wrong.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint

Cancel units explicitly. Beats cancel in heart rate × stroke volume; litres
of blood cancel in flow × oxygen-content difference.
:::

## 5. Read tissue architecture

Compare these invented descriptions: a very thin endothelial tube close to
an exchange epithelium; a round vessel with a thick muscular wall; and an
irregular partly collapsed vessel with a relatively thin wall and wide lumen.
Suggest identities, functions and limits of inference. What would distinguish
a conducting airway from a gas-exchange region in a real lung section?

## 6. Build an evidence-based comparison

In 150–200 words compare a fish's single circulation and a mammal's pulmonary/
systemic circuits. Trace the pump and exchange regions rather than simply
counting chambers. Include one consequence for pressure and one feature that
cannot be predicted from the words “open” or “closed” alone.

Finish with the [quiz](quiz.qmd).
